transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

That is probably a mechanical door-balance fault, rather than a latch or electrical problem. The usual cause is a broken or detached hinge cable or balance spring; the door then feels heavy and falls straight down instead of being supported. 1. Switch the dishwasher off at its spur/socket. Open the door slowly and support its weight. Look along both lower sides of the door/hinge area for a loose cable, displaced spring, or one side moving differently from the other. A loose or broken cable points to the balance mechanism.
2. As it is built in, also check that the furniture door has not come loose or dropped out of alignment. A misfitted heavy door panel can upset the balance, though a sudden change is more commonly a failed cable or spring.
3. Avoid letting it crash down repeatedly, as that can strain the hinges and the door-mounted wiring. If nothing is visibly out of place, it will normally need the dishwasher pulled out and the hinge/balance assembly inspected, so an appliance engineer is the sensible route. Do not try to tension springs or dismantle the hinges yourself: they are under load and access on an integrated machine is awkward.

Had a look under the plinth with a torch and I can see a loose spring hanging down on the right side. The left side still has some tension, but the right has none. Heard a twang last week when it went. Can't pull the machine out though, it's screwed to the worktop and the plinth is tight.

The loose right-hand spring, loss of tension and the twang make a failed or detached right-hand door-balance spring/cable assembly overwhelmingly likely. It is the support mechanism that has let go, which is why the door now drops. Do not try to hook or tension that spring back through the plinth opening: it is under load and can snap back, and the dishwasher needs to be pulled forward to inspect the spring, cable and hinge anchor properly. Keep supporting the door whenever it is opened and avoid letting it fall, as repeated impacts can damage the hinges or door wiring. As the machine is fixed under the worktop and cannot be withdrawn, this is an appliance-engineer job. They will need to release the fixing screws, slide the integrated dishwasher out safely, and inspect both sides; even though only the right side has visibly failed, the matching balance components are often assessed together for wear. No electrical diagnosis is indicated by these symptoms.

candidates: Worn or broken door-balance spring, cable or hinge mechanism (high)
Integrated furniture door adjustment or fitting issue (medium)

reading.symptom: door crashes down when opened and no longer stays in position

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Hotpoint.
The fault they reported is: "door crashes down when opened and no longer stays in position". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

candidates: Right-hand door-balance spring or its cable/anchor has failed or detached (high)
